source: Transcribed from A2A Simulations' own official "ACCU-SIM COMANCHE 250" Pilot's Manual PDF (a2asimulations.com/Manuals/FSX/A2A_Comanche250_Pilot's_Manual.pdf), "Normal Procedures" section. Real Piper PA-24-250 Comanche procedures, as published by the add-on's own developer; the manual's own 40-minute-runup / interactive-preflight notes are genuine current Accu-Sim product features (not legacy sim-specific cruft) and are kept. The numbered short-form checklist items are kept verbatim; the surrounding "amplified" explanatory prose is condensed into notes without changing its meaning. Cross-referenced against Flight Sim School's "A2A Comanche How To Guide" 3-part YouTube tutorial series for the video walkthrough noted in Climb/Cruise/Approach — cited by title and chapter timestamp only (verified from the videos' own chapter markers), no specific figures were taken from the videos since a reliable transcript wasn't available; all numbers here come from the manual.

items.text: When the aircraft is stopped with the engine off, press SHIFT-8 to bring up the interactive preflight inspection.

items.response: ON (LISTEN FOR PUMP, CHECK FUEL PRESSURE)
3-5 STROKES IF COLD (UNDER 40°F), NONE IF WARM

items.text: If the engine doesn't start, re-prime and repeat. If over-primed: open the throttle and turn the engine over with the starter, then re-prime with half the original amount and repeat.
Check the oil pressure gauge for an indication within 30 seconds of starting. If no pressure is shown, stop the engine and determine the trouble.

items.response: WARM UP AT 800-1200 RPM (MAX 2 MIN WARM WEATHER, 4 MIN COLD)
CHECK AT 2000 RPM (DROP NOT TO EXCEED 125 RPM, 15" MAP)
CYCLE THROUGH RANGE, LEAVE AT FULL HIGH RPM

items.text: Don't use carburetor heat on the ground in dusty conditions except momentarily during run-up — unfiltered air is drawn in and dust can damage the engine. Don't run up over loose stones or debris the propeller could pick up.

For a minimum takeoff run, lower flaps to 18° (2/3) — reduces the run by about 20%. Not normally used for crosswind takeoffs. Rotate at about 65 MPH; retract the gear once a landing could no longer be made on the remaining runway if power was lost.

Best rate of climb is 105 MPH, decreasing about 1 MPH per 1,000ft (95 MPH by 10,000ft). Below 95 MPH at low altitude cuts forward visibility and engine cooling airflow — extended climbs slower than that aren't recommended.
Video walkthrough: Flight Sim School, "A2A Comanche How To Guide Part 2: Startup To Cruise" — chapters "Climb CHT Temps" and "Climb Engine Performance".

items.response: USE ALTERNATELY (TIP TANKS FIRST, IF INSTALLED)

items.text: Maximum recommended cruise is 182 MPH. Example: 75% power at 7,000ft is 2,400 RPM / 22.6" MAP, about 14 GPH leaned to best economy (peak EGT). Cruising RPM of 2,000-2,400 with the manifold pressure for 65-75% power is recommended to balance engine wear, fuel burn and noise — see the Quick Reference power setting table for other altitudes.
Don't cruise with carburetor heat on unless icing is severe — it reduces power. Apply only briefly if needed.

Video walkthrough: Flight Sim School, "A2A Comanche How To Guide Part 2: Startup To Cruise" — chapters "Choosing A Cruise Altitude", "Cruise Power Settings", "Lean For Best Power", "Lean For Best Economy".

items.response: DOWN, UNDER 150 MPH (GREEN LIGHT ON, HORN OFF, HANDLE FORWARD)

items.text: GUMPS: Gas (pump on, tank selected) · Undercarriage (down & locked) · Mixture (rich) · Prop (high RPM) · Seatbelts (on)

Trim to about 90 MPH with full flaps, or 95 MPH with no flaps, on final. Keep the propeller at high RPM to allow a go-around if needed. For maximum braking on a short landing: full back pressure on the yoke with flaps up while braking, to load the main wheels.
Video walkthrough: Flight Sim School, "A2A Comanche How To Guide Part 3: Autopilot, Descent & Landing" — chapters "Descent & Approach" and "Landing Suggestions".
